When these mountains of afflictions fall upon someone, his falsehood is melted away, his body becomes strong, and this believer becomes accustomed to such afflictions and hardships. It is these people who are, in the end, handed the banners, and after good preparation and training, trust is placed in them again.

When such people take up this trust, it becomes dear to them with all their heart and soul, because they have made sacrifices for it and paid its heavy price. For its sake they have shown patience and endured hardships, and the worker who sacrifices his blood and his nerves, who gives up rest and tranquillity, who renounces pleasures and desirable things, and then endures torments and deprivations patiently. The truth is that it is such a worker who has awareness of this trust and this ideology, of what its worth is. Therefore he does not sell it cheaply, because he has paid its heavy price.

As for the question of whether, in the end, this faith, this trust and this Islamic ideology of life will prevail, this is the promise that Allah has made and for which He has given a guarantee. No sincere believer can doubt Allah's promise. If this promise becomes reality late, there will also be some wisdom in it, and there will be good in it for the believers. Know that Allah is more jealous for the truth, and more supportive of it, than anyone else. For the believer, trial and hardship are better, so that he may be counted among the chosen servants, become a trustee of the truth, and so that Allah may bear witness that his religion is firm and that he is fit to bear the burden of the trust, and therefore he is chosen for trial.

**Surah al-'Ankabut: At a Glance**

Surah al-'Ankabut (The Spider) is a Makki surah. Some narrations state that its first eleven verses are Madani, on the grounds that they mention jihad and the hypocrites. We, however, prefer the view that the whole surah is Makki. A narration says that its eighth verse was revealed concerning the conversion to Islam of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him), as will be mentioned shortly. There is no disagreement that Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas embraced Islam in Makkah, and clearly this verse is among those said to be Madani. Therefore, the correct position is that all these verses should be called Makki. As for the mention of jihad in them, its interpretation is simple, because from the context of the discourse it is clear that the jihad here is against trials. The jihad against the self and the mention of hypocrisy also carry this meaning, that is, the hypocrisy of a person who speaks but does not act upon what he says. These verses describe a particular type of people.

The entire surah, from beginning to end, proceeds on one line and one theme. It begins with the disjointed letters and with the faith of believers and their trials. It is stated that when faith settles in a person's heart, it makes heavy demands upon him, because faith is not merely a matter of a few words that are uttered. Rather, bearing the difficulties that come with faith and fulfilling its requirements are also part of faith, and patience upon obligations and hardships is also part of faith.

It appears that the central theme and subject of this surah is "faith and its requirements," because after the mention of faith and the hardships on the path, the stories of Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut and Shu'ayb (peace be upon them) come. Then there is mention of 'Ad, Thamud, Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman, and it is explained that from Adam (peace be upon him) onward, in all ages and nations, this same situation has been faced by the believers, that is, trials and tribulations accompany faith.

After this, it is also explained that in this world the forces of evil always place obstacles in the path of faith and create difficulties. The forces of evil display the believers in society as a contemptible force, and they ignore them, but Allah seizes them firmly.

﴿So We seized each one for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those seized by the Cry, and among them were those We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those We drowned.﴾ (29:40) At last, We seized each one for his sin. Then some of them We sent a stone-pelting wind upon, some were seized by a mighty blast, some We made the earth swallow, and some We drowned. Then a tangible example of all these forces is given, which shows how weak they are in the sight of Allah. When the powers of Allah rise, these forces are helpless.

﴿The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider, who builds a house for herself; and indeed, the frailest of houses is the house of the spider, if only they knew.﴾ (29:41)

After this, the surah connects the truth found in the message of all the prophets with the truth found in the creation of the heavens and the earth. Then all these messages are connected with the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), that they all come from Allah. All messages call to Allah alone. After this, the discussion turns to the Book of Muhammad (ﷺ), the Holy Qur'an, and it is explained what the reaction of the polytheists was regarding this Book. Despite the Book, they demand miracles that break the normal order, although the message contained in it is a mercy from Allah and the most excellent guidance and reminder. Then, in an astonishing manner, it is said that these people are hasty about the question of why the punishment does not come quickly, although Hell is about to encompass them very soon. Moreover, there is a contradiction between their own thinking and their beliefs.

﴿And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, "Allah."﴾ (29:61)

﴿And if you ask them who sends down water from the sky and with it revives the earth after its death, they will surely say, "Allah."﴾ (29:63)

﴿So when they board a ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ (29:65) Yet despite holding these beliefs, these people commit shirk and put the believers into trials.

In the midst of this debate, the believers are invited to migrate to escape these trials and not to fear death, because ﴿Every soul will taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾ (29:57) Moreover, while migrating, do not worry about what you will eat, because

﴿How many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you.﴾ (29:60) At the end of the surah, those who strive in the way of Allah are praised and extolled, and they are urged to be content with guidance and to remain steadfast.

﴿And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.﴾ (29:69) Thus the conclusion of the surah harmonizes with its beginning, and in this way the wisdom behind the entire surah becomes clear. All its parts become connected and are seen revolving around the axis of this surah.

Accordingly, the discourse of this surah on this theme moves in three rounds. In the first round, there is the reality of faith, the sunnah of Allah that He tests His workers and afflicts them with difficulties, then what the end of those who believe will be and what the end of the disbelievers will be, and that responsibility is individual. Therefore, on the Day of Resurrection no one will be able to bear the burden of another.

﴿And they will surely be asked on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate.﴾ (29:13)

In the second round, there are the stories to which we have already alluded. In these stories too, the difficulties and obstacles that always come in the path of the call and the caller are described. But in the end it is explained that these difficulties and obstacles have no significance before the powers of Allah. It is explained that the message of the messengers is based on truth, and the creation of this universe is also based on the principle of that truth. The truth upon which the universe is established and upon which religion and law are established, both come from Allah.

In the third round, it is explained that you should not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner. However, against those among them who are wrongdoers, harsh speech may be used. It may be said to the People of the Book that all religions are one, and that the religion of Islam, which the disbelievers are rejecting, is also of the same creed as all heavenly religions. Their source is one. In this round there is debate with the polytheists, and encouragement is given to those who strive in the way of Allah, so that they may be at peace, and there are glad tidings for them, and they may walk their path with steadfastness, because

﴿Indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.﴾ (29:69)

From beginning to end, throughout the discourse, there are comments scattered everywhere, through which the truth of faith is firmly planted in hearts. Through these comments, hearts are thoroughly shaken, and the hearts of the callers to truth are made to stand before the difficulties of the path of faith, so that they either endure these difficulties or abandon this path. If you do not fulfil the requirements of faith, that will be hypocrisy.

In short, these are such blows, and such strikes, which can be discussed within the context of the texts in which they occur. Therefore, we defer the detailed discussion to the explanation of the texts, and here we content ourselves with this indication.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 4:

As for those who wrong the believers, putting them to trial and committing evil deeds, they can by no means escape the punishment of Allah, even though their false powers may be flourishing and even though they may appear successful and victorious. This is Allah's promise, and in the end this is His sunnah (established way).

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they will outrun Us? Evil is their judgment.﴾ (29:4)

No corrupter should entertain the notion that he will escape or get away. If anyone thinks so, his judgment is wrong. He has miscalculated and his thinking is baseless. Allah has made the trial of the believers a sunnah, but this is so that the truthful and the liars may become evident. Part of His sunnah is also that He seizes wrongdoers, and His sunnah never changes.

At the very beginning of this surah there is a second blow: open your eyes. If it is the sunnah of Allah to put the believers through the furnace of trial and to distinguish the genuine from the counterfeit, then seizing the wrongdoers and corrupters is also the sunnah of Allah, so make preparations for that as well. Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, let him be assured and wait for what Allah has promised them. This waiting should be of the kind in which one has firm certainty that the thing will be received, and is watching for it. Only the coming of the day is awaited, and the longing for the meeting keeps growing. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (29:5).

"." When Allah sets trials for the believers and commands them to bear these hardships, so that their souls become capable of bearing difficulties in the arena of life, then these commands are also for the reform of the believers themselves. He rises above love of wealth and love of self; now the noble qualities of his personality unfold and his capacities come to the fore. No one should begin jihad and then, midway, stand up saying, "Come now, pay me for the jihad so far," or hold a favour over Allah, or hold a favour over the Islamic movement, or say, "What have we gained from all this effort?" This is such a great reward that, even if they do not receive justice throughout their entire life in this world, it is sufficient for them.

ووصینا الانسان بوالدیہ ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ فی الصلحین (8 – 9)

Parents are the closest of all relatives and the most worthy of respect. Regarding them, a child should become embodiment of kindness, and according to the Shariah, showing them mercy and respect has been made obligatory. ووصینا الانسان ۔۔۔۔۔۔ فلا تطعھما (29: 8) "We have enjoined upon man to be good to his parents; but if they strive to make you associate with Me something of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them."

Because the believer's first bond is with Allah, and this bond and connection is unbreakable. If the parents are polytheists or disbelievers, then only good treatment will be shown to them; respect and consideration will be maintained, but their following will not be. In this brief worldly life this is how it will be; the real matter is the Hereafter, where both will be before Allah.

والذین امنوا ۔۔۔۔۔ فی الصلحین (29: 9) "Those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous." Thus the people of Allah will be one community, just as in reality they are one community. Lineage, blood and kinship will end there. These things will remain here in this world. These are the temporary ties of this world, and those who have been cut off from that true bond, namely the bond of faith, will be annihilated in the Hereafter.

Imam Tirmidhi has narrated a report that this verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him) and his mother Hamna bint Abi Sufyan. He used to treat his mother with great kindness. She said to him, "What is this religion you have adopted? By Allah, I will neither eat nor drink until you abandon this religion, or until I die. Thus people will taunt you throughout your life, and people will say, 'O slayer of your mother!'" She carried out a hunger strike for twenty-four hours. Then Sa'd came to her and said, "O mother, even if you had a hundred lives and you gave up one life after another, I would still not abandon my religion. If you wish, eat and drink; if you do not wish, continue your hunger strike." When she despaired that he would not give in, she began to eat and drink. Then Allah revealed this verse: be good to your parents, but do not obey them in associating partners with Allah.

Thus in this incident, faith prevailed over the closest bond of lineage, yet the Qur'an continued to enjoin good treatment towards relatives and parents. The believers face such trials in every age. Therefore this verse and this hadith of Sa'd are signposts for us. This is the path of peace and salvation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 10–11:

Now, in connection with the difficulties of the path of faith, there is another character: when difficulties come, he cries out and wails, but when success and victories come from Allah, he then makes lengthy and boastful claims. Allah, in a few words, highlights this character too, so that a clear picture comes before us.

﴿And among people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah...﴾ up to ﴿...and Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.﴾ (10–11)

Such characters are common among people. Such people take the word "iman" (faith) lightly and profess it, thinking that it carries no responsibility. They think that it only means reciting the kalimah with the tongue, and that it has no requirements. But when hardships come upon them for the sake of Allah's path, and this trial comes because of that kalimah, then

﴿He considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah﴾ (29:10). He considers this trial to be the punishment of Allah. He begins to lament and wail, and his religious values change. His belief becomes shaky. He says that this is indeed the punishment of Hell, and that we are in Hell. He thinks that this is indeed the painful punishment, so what need is there to remain firm on faith? After all, what could Hell be worse than the calamity we are in? This is the way he thinks. He considers this minor worldly suffering to be the punishment of Allah, whereas in Hell there will be a punishment that we cannot even imagine, and it will have no limits... This was his character in trial. But if there is happiness...

﴿And if a victory comes from your Lord, he will surely say, "We were with you"﴾ (29:10). "We were with you." And see how light, contemptible he was in difficulties, and how false his assessments and estimations were... Now he is making lengthy and boastful claims, he cannot contain his pride, and now he says:

﴿"We were with you"﴾ (29:10). And the answer comes well:

﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds?﴾ (29:10) Is not the film of your hearts present with Allah? Allah knows who remained patient and who wailed, who is a believer and who is a hypocrite. Do they wish to deceive Allah?

﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites﴾ (29:11). Allah wants to expose them, and they will certainly continue to be exposed. Trials come precisely so that the genuine and the counterfeit are separated. The words the Qur'an uses here about this hypocritical character deserve reflection. These words point to where this character went wrong.

﴿He considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah﴾ (29:10). Their mistake is not that, when hardship came upon them, their patience was exhausted in bearing it, for at times even a truly sincere believer may not be able to bear it, since human strength has its limits. Rather, a truly sincere believer does distinguish between the harms that come from people and the punishment of Allah. He cannot err to such an extent that something of this transient world and something of the eternal world of the Hereafter could be considered equal. Even the unbearable punishment of this world is nothing compared to the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. In the consciousness of the believer, nothing can be equal to Allah and His incomparable work. This is the difference between the believer and the hypocrite.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 12–13:

At the end comes the example of the trial of misleading and misguiding people. It is shown that the disbelievers' notion regarding reward and punishment is somewhat baseless, since a person who misleads another then takes upon himself the responsibility of the Hereafter, whereas with Allah it is the fundamental principle that every person is personally responsible for what he does. This is a supreme form of justice which Islam established clearly. It is the golden principle of justice.

﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe: "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins."﴾ (12–13)

This statement, these people made according to that unjust principle in which responsibility for crimes was collective. The whole tribe would be responsible for a crime. Under this wrong custom, they also imagined that they could take upon themselves the responsibility for shirk in the Hereafter and thus save those others from the punishment for their sin. In fact, they were mocking the reward and punishment of the Hereafter.

﴿Follow our way, and we will bear your sins﴾ (29:12): "Follow our path and we will bear your wrongs." For this reason, the decisive answer is today: every person will certainly be presented before Allah. Every person will be called to account for his deeds, and no one will be responsible for the deeds of another.

﴿And they are not in the least bearers of their sins﴾ (29:12): "though they will by no means bear anything of their sins." It is shown that their boasting is false, and that they are liars in it.

﴿Indeed, they are liars﴾ (29:12): "Surely they are lying."

Yes, these people will bear the burden of their own misguidance, they will bear the burden of shirk, they will bear the burden of this fabrication, and they will bear the burden of misguiding others, when those who were misguided will not be forgiven either.

﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens, and other burdens along with their burdens; and on the Day of Resurrection they will surely be questioned about what they used to fabricate﴾ (29:13). Thus the door of this trial and temptation is closed forever, and it is declared that people's reckoning will not be collective but individual, and every person will be responsible for what he has done.

﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned﴾ ("Every person will be a pledge for the wealth he has earned").

Lesson No. 181: At a Glance

In the previous round it was explained that those who profess the word of faith will certainly be tested according to Allah's enduring sunnah, and will be afflicted with hardships, so that a distinction may be made between the truthful and the liars. The trials include the trial of persecution, the trial through relatives, and the trial of conspiracies and temptations.

In this lesson the trials are mentioned that have been faced by the leaders of every Islamic call from the time of Nuh (peace be upon him) onward, whether they were prophets or their followers and companions. In this history of calling and steadfast resolve, the circumstances of Ibrahim and Lut (peace be upon both of them) are taken up in some detail, while the circumstances of the other prophets are described in brief.

These narratives show that many kinds of difficulties and obstacles came in the way of the Islamic call. In the story of Nuh (peace be upon him) it is related that he struggled for a long time and the result was very meagre. In the course of nine hundred and fifty years of struggle, very few became Muslims.

﴿فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفَانُ وَهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾ (29:14) "Then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers."

Against the call of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the rebellious ruler returned him with persecution, although he had striven as far as he could for their guidance. When he spoke with reasonable arguments, the response of that people was also this:

﴿فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَن قَالُوا اقْتُلُوهُ أَوْ حَرِّقُوهُ﴾ (29:24) "So the answer of his people was nothing but that they said, 'Kill him or burn him.'" The story of Lut shows how stubborn these vile people had become, and how shameless and ungrateful they had turned. They did not show any regard or respect even for the Prophet, they had reduced humanity below the level of the animals, they had become immersed in filth and vices, and they dared to act thus against their warner and sympathiser.

﴿فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَن قَالُوا ائْتِنَا بِعَذَابِ اللَّهِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ (29:29) "The answer of his people was nothing but that they said, 'Bring us the punishment of Allah if you are among the truthful.'"

In the story of Shu'ayb, too, corruption and rebellion from the people of Madyan come to the fore, and they turn away from truth and reality and deny it.

﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ﴾ (29:37) "Then a violent earthquake seized them, and they lay prostrate in their homes by morning."

Reference is made to the display of pride, power and arrogance by the people of ʿĀd and Thamūd. Likewise, reference is made to Pharaoh, Qarun and Haman, who regarded wealth, government, conspiracy and arrogance as the source of strength against the truth. On all these historical powers the Qur'an comments that these powers, however forceful they may be, when they confront the truth their standing becomes equal to a spider's web.

﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ كَمَثَلِ الْعَنكَبُوتِ اتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ الْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ الْعَنكَبُوتِ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (29:41) "The likeness of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider, which makes for itself a house; and indeed the frailest of houses is the spider's house, if they but knew."

Lesson 181: Commentary on the Verses

14 to 44

﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفَانُ وَهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ * فَأَنجَيْنَاهُ وَأَصْحَابَ السَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلْنَاهَا آيَةً لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ (29:14–15) "And We certainly sent Nuh to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years. Then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers. So We saved him and the companions of the ark, and made it a sign for the worlds."

Nuh (peace be upon him) gave da'wah for nine hundred and fifty years. Some part of his life before he was granted prophethood may have passed, the extent of which is not specified here, and he also lived on after the flood, and that period too is not specified. Thus the age of Nuh (peace be upon him) apparently appears to be much greater than the ordinary natural lifespan, but this age has been stated by the Qur'an, which is the most true source of knowledge in this universe, and for its truth it is sufficient that it is the explicit statement of the Qur'an. Its explanation may be this: at that time the hand of divine power granted long lives so that the earth would be populated and the race would spread. When people became numerous, the need for long life no longer remained. This principle is seen to operate in several living things: where the number of a living kind is small, its lifespan is greater. For example, birds of prey such as the falcon, and tortoises, whose lifespans are still hundreds of years, while the housefly lives at most about two weeks. A poet has said well:

بعاث الطير أكثرها فراخا وأم الصقر مقلاة نزور

"The weak birds have many chicks, but the mother of the falcon is one who bears very few young."

For this reason the falcon has a long lifespan, and smaller birds that bear more young have short lifespans. The works of Allah are based on wisdom, and with Him everything is in measure. In any case, as a result of Nuh's nine hundred and fifty years of preaching, only a small number entered Islam, and the majority, because of their oppression, were swept away by the flood. Since they persisted in such long obstinacy and rebellion, Allah destroyed them and saved the small number who were believers. These were the people of the ark. From them the human lineage continued afterwards. And the flood became a sign for all the worlds, and for a long time the outcome of oppression, shirk and disbelief was remembered through the story of Nuh.

After wrapping up the centuries of history following Nuh, the Qur'an takes up the events of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 16–18:

وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ ... عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ (16–18)

Hazrat Ibrahim (alayhis salam) gave his people a very clear and simple invitation, in which there was no complexity or vagueness. He presented this invitation in a highly orderly manner. Those who carry on the work of Islamic da'wah should reflect on this order and method of da'wah. First, he placed the reality of his invitation before them.

اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ (29:16) "Worship Allah and fear Him."

After this, he created in their hearts an interest in this invitation, that there is much good for you in it, provided you understand good and evil and recognise the places of good.

ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (29:16) "That is better for you, if you only knew."

In this conditional sequence, they are encouraged to abandon ignorance and, by negating ignorance regarding their own selves, to adopt the path of good for themselves. This is also a reality; it is not mere rhetoric, nor a stubbornness born of oratorical excitement, nor mere wordplay.

In the third stage, they are told that the beliefs and ideologies they hold are wrong in many respects. They worship idols, and these idols are made of stone or wood. This worship is an extremely false and worthless act, and it also prevents them from worshipping Allah alone. Moreover, there is no sound proof or argument for what they worship; rather, these are false statements which they have fabricated themselves. They have neither a precedent nor a basis; they are false, self-invented claims, not founded on any accepted principle or rule. Furthermore, these idols can neither benefit nor harm them, nor can they give them anything.

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ ... لَكُمْ رِزْقًا (29:17) "Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not have the power to provide you any sustenance."

In the fourth stage, the Qur'an again directs them to seek sustenance from Allah, for He alone is the Sustainer. This matter is very important for them, and their needs and necessities can be fulfilled only at the court of Allah.

فَابْتَغُوا عِندَ اللَّهِ الرِّزْقَ (29:17) "So seek your sustenance from Allah."

Sustenance is in fact the concern of souls, especially of believing souls, and seeking sustenance from Allah alone is also a reality. It is not mere psychological agitation, nor a psychological inclination being stirred up, but a reality.

Finally, they are invited to worship the true Causer and true Benefactor of blessings and provisions, and to give thanks to Him.

وَاعْبُدُوهُ وَاشْكُرُوا لَهُ (29:17) "Worship Him and be grateful to Him."

Finally, they are told that they cannot escape from Him, nor can they find refuge from Allah anywhere. Therefore, the proper course, and that which is for their good, is that they return to Him, believe, worship Him, and give thanks to Him.

إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ (29:17) "To Him you will be returned."

And if, after this invitation, they deny you, what is the significance of that denial? Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 19–23:

اولم یروا کیف ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ واولئک لھم عذاب الیم (19 – 23)

This is addressed to everyone who denies Allah and denies accountability before Him. The entire universe is presented here as proof for this address. The scope of this argument extends to the heavens and the earth. It is the well-known style of argument of the Qur'an that it turns the whole universe into an exhibition of the signs and proofs of Allah, and invites the human heart and sight to seek in this open book the signs and proofs of Allah: to seek the truth of Allah's existence, His oneness, and the truth of His promise and warning. These observations and manifestations of the universe are open before our eyes at all times and are present. They are commonplace, but because a person sees them constantly, he becomes accustomed to them, and the aspect of their miraculous nature escapes his sight; and because these miracles are repeated again and again, they have little effect on the human heart and sight. It is the excellence of the Qur'an that it revives these commonplace scenes and proofs of miraculousness afresh and presents them in a beautiful form, and they become so lovely, beautiful and impactful that a person feels as if these sights and scenes are being presented before him for the first time. These scenes come before him in a living form and affect the human heart and sight, and a person draws the effects and consequences from them, and these very scenes become proofs and demonstrations for human intuition, and human consciousness is deeply affected by them. This style of argument is not like dry logical argument, which consists merely of outward disputation and a lifeless style of discourse. This philosophical and logical style of argument has always been unfamiliar to Islamic logic and consciousness. Therefore, Islamic consciousness has never been deeply influenced by it. The Islamic style of argument is this:

اولم یروا کیف ۔۔۔۔۔۔ اللہ یسیر (29: 19) "Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah." Indeed these people see how Allah creates; this creation is visible even in a small plant, it is visible in an egg and in an embryo. And it is visible in everything that did not exist and then came into existence, and none of these things is such that a person, either individually or collectively, even if he strives, can create a thing like it, nor can they claim that they are its creator. The creations of Allah are many; the miracle of life alone is a continuous miracle. How did life come into being? This too is a miracle; to claim the invention of life by anyone is a great matter. Regarding life, a person can only say that it is created by Allah. Allah repeats it every moment, and people see it with their own eyes and cannot even deny it.

People see that Allah is bringing people into existence, so the re-creation of these things is extremely easy for Allah.

ان ذلک علی اللہ یسیر (29: 19) "And this (re-creation) is easier for Allah." Nothing among Allah's creations is difficult for Allah. But Allah speaks to them according to human standards, because among human productions, repeating a thing is easier than the first making of it; otherwise, for Allah, beginning and repeating are equal. When Allah wills to create something, He directs His will and says "Be," and it is.

After this, Allah invites these people: go about the earth with open eyes, and look at the signs and manifestations of Allah. Reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation in living and non-living things, and you will come to know that Allah's creation is also taking place automatically, without any hardship. And the re-creation will also be in the same way.

قل سیرو فی الارض ۔۔۔۔۔ کل شئ قدیر (29: 20) "Say: Travel through the earth and see how He originated creation. Then Allah will bring about the later creation. Indeed, Allah is capable of everything."

Travelling through the earth increases a person's insight and sight. A person sees scenes that his eye has never seen and that his heart has never reflected upon. In this verse, Allah has drawn our attention to a profound truth. A person lives in a region and its scenes and wonders are hidden from his sight, but when he travels, his feelings and perceptive faculties observe every new scene closely. In a new world and region, new scenes and sights impress him. Although similar and even better scenes exist in his own region, he never even looks at them. When he returns to his homeland, he sees his own dwelling with fresh feeling and fresh reflection. Previously he gave no importance to the things that he now, after being away for a few days, looks upon with affection and rejoices in. Now these scenes and wonders speak to him anew, whereas previously these wonders were neither strange to him nor spoke to him.

Glory be to Him who revealed this Qur'an, who knows the paths of the heart through which the inner world can be influenced, and who is also acquainted with the ways of the realm of the self.

قل سیروا فی الارض ۔۔۔۔۔ الخلق (29: 20) "Say: Travel through the earth and see how He originated creation." Here the beginning of creation is described through the past tense.

کیف بدا الخلق (29: 20) "How did He originate creation?" And you should learn this by travelling through the earth and touring. From this it becomes clear that by travelling through the earth you should learn about the beginning of Allah's creation, and reflect on the things through which the initial state of "life" may be known, how life began in this world. Nowadays some scholars of archaeology dig into the earth to learn the condition of the initial creation: how life began, how it developed, and how it spread. Despite these discoveries, these scholars have still not reached the reality of "life": what life is, where it comes from, and how the first living human or creature came to this world. All these investigations and all these traces will in fact be proofs of re-creation.

And along with this thought, there is another thought: that the people to whom the Qur'an was revealed were not capable of learning the traces and conditions of the beginning of life, as people today have become capable of observing the traces and conditions of the beginning of life. Therefore, if the meaning of this verse is this, then those people were not capable of it; hence the Qur'an was asking its first addressees to learn something else that they could learn, and from learning which they could draw the conclusion of the possibility of the resurrection. Therefore, what was required of them would be that they observe the beginning of the creation of plants, animals and humans everywhere, travel through the earth, and that this travel and observation sharpen their power of observation, as we explained in the first paragraph: that they observe the manifestations of divine power, and reflect upon the miracles and signs that the power of Allah displays through night and day.

Another possibility, which is in accordance with the method of the Qur'an, is that the Qur'an addresses the people of every age according to their circumstances, according to their rank and position in knowledge and culture, according to their conditions of life, and according to their present means of discovery; they should reflect, according to their own circumstances, on the proofs of divine power found in this universe. In this way, with the development of life's conditions, there will also be progress in the understanding and comprehension of the meaning of the Qur'an, and there will be no contradiction between the two ideas, and this meaning is closer to the method of the Qur'an.

ان اللہ علی کل شئ قدیر (29: 20) "Indeed, Allah is capable of everything." Allah begins this life and will also repeat it, and this will happen through His overpowering might. The powers of Allah are not confined within the limits of human thought, nor can the powers of Allah be confined within the bounds of human thinking and possibilities, because human thought is limited to human limited experiences.

This is why Allah says that He is capable of everything. He punishes whom He wills and brings whom He wills within the circle of His mercy. All people will ultimately return to Him, and nothing can prevent Allah from doing this deed, nor can anyone forbid Him.

یعذب من یشآء ۔۔۔۔۔۔ ولی ولا نصیر (29: 21 – 22)

"He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned. You cannot escape (Him) on the earth or in the heaven, and you have no protector or helper besides Allah."

Mercy and punishment are both subject to Allah's mercy, in such a way that Allah has explained the path of guidance and misguidance, and has created in man the capacity to choose whichever path of guidance or misguidance he wishes. He has made both paths available to man. Now it is up to the human being which way he adopts. However, if he adopts the path of Allah, then Allah has made it binding upon Himself to assist such a person; and if he turns away from Allah's proofs and stops from Allah's path, then he cuts off his connection with Allah, and as a result of this principle, mercy and punishment from Allah reach people.

والیہ تقلبون (29: 21) "And to Him you will be returned." "You cannot escape (Him) on the earth or in the heaven." You have no such power that you could prevent the entire creation from returning to Allah, neither on earth nor in the heavens. Jinn and angels are not your power either.

وما لکم ۔۔۔۔۔ ولا نصیر (29: 22) "And you have no protector or helper besides Allah." Who is a guardian and helper besides Allah? Where is he? Is he an angel or a jinn? They are all themselves servants of Allah and creations of Allah. They do not own their own benefit or harm; what can they do for others?

والذین کفروا ۔۔۔۔۔۔ عذاب الیم (29: 23) "Those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and in meeting Him, they have despaired of My mercy, and for them there is a painful punishment."

This is because a person despairs of Allah's mercy only when his heart is disbelieving. In such a situation, the connection between him and his Lord is then severed. Whoever adopts the path of disbelief has already had his connection with his Lord cut off. There is no freshness in his personality. Therefore he finds no way to enter into Allah's mercy. And then his end is also determined.

اولئک لھم عذاب الیم (29: 23) "For such people there is a painful punishment."

After this thought-provoking point, now comes the response from the people of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him). This incidental address was for the reflection of everyone who rejects the call to faith. That response is extremely disappointing and strange, and it shows how those who hold disbelief and rebellion become self-deluded, because they possess the power of authority.

This is addressed to everyone who denies Allah and denies accountability before Him. The entire universe is presented here as proof for this address. The scope of this argument extends to the heavens and the earth. It is the well-known style of argument of the Qur'an that it turns the whole universe into an exhibition of the signs and proofs of Allah, and invites the human heart and sight to seek in this open book the signs and proofs of Allah: to seek the truth of Allah's existence, His oneness, and the truth of His promise and warning. These observations and manifestations of the universe are open before our eyes at all times and are present. They are commonplace, but because a person sees them constantly, he becomes accustomed to them, and the aspect of their miraculous nature escapes his sight; and because these miracles are repeated again and again, they have little effect on the human heart and sight. It is the excellence of the Qur'an that it revives these commonplace scenes and proofs of miraculousness afresh and presents them in a beautiful form, and they become so lovely, beautiful and impactful that a person feels as if these sights and scenes are being presented before him for the first time. These scenes come before him in a living form and affect the human heart and sight, and a person draws the effects and consequences from them, and these very scenes become proofs and demonstrations for human intuition, and human consciousness is deeply affected by them. This style of argument is not like dry logical argument, which consists merely of outward disputation and a lifeless style of discourse. This philosophical and logical style of argument has always been unfamiliar to Islamic logic and consciousness. Therefore, Islamic consciousness has never been deeply influenced by it. The Islamic style of argument is this:

اولم یروا کیف ۔۔۔۔۔۔ اللہ یسیر (29: 19) "Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah." Indeed these people see how Allah creates; this creation is visible even in a small plant, it is visible in an egg and in an embryo. And it is visible in everything that did not exist and then came into existence, and none of these things is such that a person, either individually or collectively, even if he strives, can create a thing like it, nor can they claim that they are its creator. The creations of Allah are many; the miracle of life alone is a continuous miracle. How did life come into being? This too is a miracle; to claim the invention of life by anyone is a great matter. Regarding life, a person can only say that it is created by Allah. Allah repeats it every moment, and people see it with their own eyes and cannot even deny it.

People see that Allah is bringing people into existence, so the re-creation of these things is extremely easy for Allah.

ان ذلک علی اللہ یسیر (29: 19) "And this (re-creation) is easier for Allah." Nothing among Allah's creations is difficult for Allah. But Allah speaks to them according to human standards, because among human productions, repeating a thing is easier than the first making of it; otherwise, for Allah, beginning and repeating are equal. When Allah wills to create something, He directs His will and says "Be," and it is.

After this, Allah invites these people: go about the earth with open eyes, and look at the signs and manifestations of Allah. Reflect on the wonders of Allah's creation in living and non-living things, and you will come to know that Allah's creation is also taking place automatically, without any hardship. And the re-creation will also be in the same way.

قل سیرو فی الارض ۔۔۔۔۔ کل شئ قدیر (29: 20) "Say: Travel through the earth and see how He originated creation. Then Allah will bring about the later creation. Indeed, Allah is capable of everything."

Travelling through the earth increases a person's insight and sight. A person sees scenes that his eye has never seen and that his heart has never reflected upon. In this verse, Allah has drawn our attention to a profound truth. A person lives in a region and its scenes and wonders are hidden from his sight, but when he travels, his feelings and perceptive faculties observe every new scene closely. In a new world and region, new scenes and sights impress him. Although similar and even better scenes exist in his own region, he never even looks at them. When he returns to his homeland, he sees his own dwelling with fresh feeling and fresh reflection. Previously he gave no importance to the things that he now, after being away for a few days, looks upon with affection and rejoices in. Now these scenes and wonders speak to him anew, whereas previously these wonders were neither strange to him nor spoke to him.

Glory be to Him who revealed this Qur'an, who knows the paths of the heart through which the inner world can be influenced, and who is also acquainted with the ways of the realm of the self.

قل سیروا فی الارض ۔۔۔۔۔ الخلق (29: 20) "Say: Travel through the earth and see how He originated creation." Here the beginning of creation is described through the past tense.

کیف بدا الخلق (29: 20) "How did He originate creation?" And you should learn this by travelling through the earth and touring. From this it becomes clear that by travelling through the earth you should learn about the beginning of Allah's creation, and reflect on the things through which the initial state of "life" may be known, how life began in this world. Nowadays some scholars of archaeology dig into the earth to learn the condition of the initial creation: how life began, how it developed, and how it spread. Despite these discoveries, these scholars have still not reached the reality of "life": what life is, where it comes from, and how the first living human or creature came to this world. All these investigations and all these traces will in fact be proofs of re-creation.

And along with this thought, there is another thought: that the people to whom the Qur'an was revealed were not capable of learning the traces and conditions of the beginning of life, as people today have become capable of observing the traces and conditions of the beginning of life. Therefore, if the meaning of this verse is this, then those people were not capable of it; hence the Qur'an was asking its first addressees to learn something else that they could learn, and from learning which they could draw the conclusion of the possibility of the resurrection. Therefore, what was required of them would be that they observe the beginning of the creation of plants, animals and humans everywhere, travel through the earth, and that this travel and observation sharpen their power of observation, as we explained in the first paragraph: that they observe the manifestations of divine power, and reflect upon the miracles and signs that the power of Allah displays through night and day.

Another possibility, which is in accordance with the method of the Qur'an, is that the Qur'an addresses the people of every age according to their circumstances, according to their rank and position in knowledge and culture, according to their conditions of life, and according to their present means of discovery; they should reflect, according to their own circumstances, on the proofs of divine power found in this universe. In this way, with the development of life's conditions, there will also be progress in the understanding and comprehension of the meaning of the Qur'an, and there will be no contradiction between the two ideas, and this meaning is closer to the method of the Qur'an.

ان اللہ علی کل شئ قدیر (29: 20) "Indeed, Allah is capable of everything." Allah begins this life and will also repeat it, and this will happen through His overpowering might. The powers of Allah are not confined within the limits of human thought, nor can the powers of Allah be confined within the bounds of human thinking and possibilities, because human thought is limited to human limited experiences.

This is why Allah says that He is capable of everything. He punishes whom He wills and brings whom He wills within the circle of His mercy. All people will ultimately return to Him, and nothing can prevent Allah from doing this deed, nor can anyone forbid Him.

یعذب من یشآء ۔۔۔۔۔۔ ولی ولا نصیر (29: 21 – 22)

"He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned. You cannot escape (Him) on the earth or in the heaven, and you have no protector or helper besides Allah."

Mercy and punishment are both subject to Allah's mercy, in such a way that Allah has explained the path of guidance and misguidance, and has created in man the capacity to choose whichever path of guidance or misguidance he wishes. He has made both paths available to man. Now it is up to the human being which way he adopts. However, if he adopts the path of Allah, then Allah has made it binding upon Himself to assist such a person; and if he turns away from Allah's proofs and stops from Allah's path, then he cuts off his connection with Allah, and as a result of this principle, mercy and punishment from Allah reach people.

والیہ تقلبون (29: 21) "And to Him you will be returned." "You cannot escape (Him) on the earth or in the heaven." You have no such power that you could prevent the entire creation from returning to Allah, neither on earth nor in the heavens. Jinn and angels are not your power either.

وما لکم ۔۔۔۔۔ ولا نصیر (29: 22) "And you have no protector or helper besides Allah." Who is a guardian and helper besides Allah? Where is he? Is he an angel or a jinn? They are all themselves servants of Allah and creations of Allah. They do not own their own benefit or harm; what can they do for others?

والذین کفروا ۔۔۔۔۔۔ عذاب الیم (29: 23) "Those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and in meeting Him, they have despaired of My mercy, and for them there is a painful punishment."

This is because a person despairs of Allah's mercy only when his heart is disbelieving. In such a situation, the connection between him and his Lord is then severed. Whoever adopts the path of disbelief has already had his connection with his Lord cut off. There is no freshness in his personality. Therefore he finds no way to enter into Allah's mercy. And then his end is also determined.

اولئک لھم عذاب الیم (29: 23) "For such people there is a painful punishment."

After this thought-provoking point, now comes the response from the people of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him). This incidental address was for the reflection of everyone who rejects the call to faith. That response is extremely disappointing and strange, and it shows how those who hold disbelief and rebellion become self-deluded, because they possess the power of authority.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ (29:24). The first sign is that Ibrahim was saved from the fire. The third lesson is that if Allah does not wish to guide someone, then miracles also are of no benefit. And these signs are for those who reflect upon the history of the Islamic call, and who seek to understand who it is that turns hearts and what the causes of guidance and misguidance are.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 25:

After the rescue of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the story moves forward. Ibrahim now despaired of the guidance of a people who did not believe even after seeing such a clear and manifest miracle. Before he bid them farewell, he places them, as a final proof, before a reality:

﴿And he said, "You have taken, instead of Allah, idols as a means of affection among yourselves in the life of this world; but on the Day of Resurrection, you will deny one another and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers."﴾ (29:25)

We did not adopt the worship of idols because you believe them to be gods in conviction, and you are content with their worship. Rather, you have agreed upon this evil out of regard for one another's feelings, and you worship them merely by agreeing with one another. Not one of you friends wishes to abandon the gods of the others, even though the truth has become clear. If someone accepts a new truth, there is a danger that these friendships will end. You maintain these friendships by doing injustice to the truth. You disregard the truth and give greater importance to friendships in comparison with it. You disregard the truth and give greater importance to friendships in comparison with it, although the Islamic call is a serious matter. It accepts neither mere talk, nor compromise, nor any friendship.

After this, the pages of their otherworldly end are opened. The friends for whose sake they disregard the truth and remain in the worship of idols will, on the Day of Resurrection, become enemies to one another. They will curse and revile one another and blame one another, and these friendships will be broken.

﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others and curse one another﴾ (29:25): "But this cursing and reviling will benefit them nothing. It will not lessen your punishment in any way."

﴿And your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers﴾ (29:25): "In that very Fire, these people will remain, the same Fire with which they wished to burn Ibrahim. But Allah helped him and granted him deliverance. As for them, there is neither help nor deliverance for them."

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) gave up calling his people. This undeniable miracle also came before them. As a result of this call and this irrefutable miracle, only one person accepted Islam: Lut. Lut's wife also did not accept Islam. Some narrations state that Lut was the nephew of Ibrahim. This one Muslim migrated with Ibrahim from the city of Ur of the Iranians, and after passing beyond Jordan they settled in the region ahead.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 26–30:

Fa-amana lahu Lut... ʿala al-qawm al-mufsidin (26–30)

The words of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) deserve reflection. He says:

﴿Inni muhajirun ila rabbi﴾ (29:26), "I am migrating to my Lord."

Why did he migrate? He did not migrate for the sake of salvation. He did not migrate to acquire land, nor for the sake of trade and earnings. He migrated to his Lord, to draw near to Allah and to take refuge in His protection. He migrated with his heart and his conviction. His heart and mind migrated before his body and blood did. He migrated to Allah so that he might worship and serve Him alone, dedicating his body and his thinking to Him, and leaving behind the land of disbelief and misguidance, because for the people of that land there was no longer any prospect of guidance. Allah rewarded Ibrahim (peace be upon him) for leaving that land even in this world. He granted him righteous offspring who became the inheritors of his legacy and his principles for the rest of the world. After this, prophethood remained among his descendants. There is no greater reward in this world or in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 27:

﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and placed in his offspring prophethood and the Book...﴾ (29:27)

This is a blessing of Allah from which the springs of bounty and blessing flow, and in which Allah's good pleasure is manifest. In the person of this blessed prophet, this bounty was evident, even though all the rebellious and insolent powers gathered to burn him, yet Allah, in a magnificent miraculous manner, made his environment cool and full of peace. This was Allah's kindness, His generosity, and a fitting reward for the people of tawhid. After this brief account of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the story of Lut now comes. He migrated with Ibrahim (peace be upon him) towards his Lord. Both of them settled in the valley of Jordan. Lut began to call a people by the shore of the Dead Sea. After that, that lake came to be named the Lake of Lut. He was appointed in the city of Sodom. Lut intermarried with these people and also engaged in economic activity among them.

An strange moral sickness spread among this people. The Qur'an states that this abominable disease had not spread among any people before them. That these people began to establish sexual relations with men, in place of women and to the exclusion of women. Whereas Allah had created women for this very purpose, so that a family would come into existence from a man and a woman, and thus the continuity of human life would remain established naturally. Just as this system is established among all other living creatures, since Allah created all animals and plants in pairs: men and women, male and female. In short, this disease had not arisen among any other people before the people of Lut.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 29, verse 28–30:

ولوطا اذقال لقومہ ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ علی القوم المفسدین (28: 29 – 30) ” ۔ “۔ “۔

From the speech of Hadrat Lut it appears that these people had sunk up to their ears in this evil. They had fallen into an evil which no human being had committed before them. They would establish sexual relations with men. It was a strange and filthy act. This shows that the very nature of these people had changed. Whenever any nation abandons moderation (i'tidal), its nature changes, because pure sexual relations are established only with a woman. Therefore it was declared an extremely abominable crime. Sexual relations with a woman also sometimes exceed the limits and bounds, but it remains, after all, a natural act. As for homosexuality, it is an act lower than even animals. There is corruption in it from the standpoint of the natural physical composition of man, and also corruption from the psychological standpoint. The pleasure that exists in the relationship between spouses is in harmony with the great purpose of the continuation of life. As a result, the continuity of human life is maintained, and both partners enjoy this relationship physically and spiritually, and there is physical and organic harmony in their union and coupling. As for the relationship that the people of Lut used to establish, it was unnatural, unpleasant and purposeless. If anyone finds pleasure in this relationship, it becomes known that the nature of such people has been corrupted, distorted and is not in accordance with reality. These people also committed robbery along with this evil; by frightening people they would extract financial benefits from them. Then they would commit this act by compelling men. This was a further hideous form of this evil act: along with plunder, they would commit this indecency with people.

Then they would commit this disgraceful act in their gatherings, openly and collectively. They did not feel any shame in doing it to one another, like dogs. This is the worst degree of obscenity. It is the extreme of corruption of nature, and such pride in vices that after this no hope of reform remains.

Here the story has been brought in brief. It is evident that at first Hadrat Lut must have forbidden them in the most gentle manner. They must have insisted. Hadrat Lut must have warned them of the punishment of Allah and told them that this is a very abominable act and its end will also be frightening and a lesson.

﴿Then the answer of his people was none but that they said: Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful.﴾ (29: 29) This is the arrogance and insolence in face of a warning prophet, a denial in the manner of a challenge, and it is a corruption from which no good is expected and no hope of reform remains. The Messenger of God completed the proof against them, and there remained no way except that they seek help from Allah, who is the final support.

﴿He said: My Lord, help me against the corrupt people.﴾ (29: 30) Now the curtain falls here. On the scene, only Lut (peace be upon him) is seen praying. Now there comes before us the scene of the acceptance of this prayer. Those whom the angels were commanded to overturn Sodom upside down, they had also given the good news to Hadrat Ibrahim before that act: the good news of a righteous son from a wife who was barren.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 29, verse 31–32:

Wa lamma ja'at rusulunā Ibrāhīma ... kānat min al-ghābirīn (31–32)

This scene, the scene of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and the angels, was not the primary focus here, so it has been taken up with great brevity. In the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) elsewhere, it is mentioned that he was given the good news of Ishaq and Ya'qub. The birth of Ishaq was itself the subject of glad tidings. Therefore these matters have not been detailed here, because the aim is the completion of the story of Lut. Here it is simply stated that the angels came to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) in order to give him good news and to inform him of the mission on which they had come.

Inna muhlikū ahl ... zālimīn (29:31) "We are about to destroy the people of this town; its people are severe wrongdoers." Now the feeling of mercy and love of Ibrahim welled up. He immediately said that Lut, his nephew, also lives there, and that he is not a wrongdoer but a righteous man. The angels and messengers of Allah replied that they had been given complete information about this mission and that they know all matters.

Qālū naḥnu a'lam ... min al-ghābirīn (29:32) "They said: We know very well who is there. We will save him and his family, except his wife; she is among those who remain behind." This wife was with the people (of the town). She also affirmed their crimes and evil deeds, and it was a strange thing that a woman should commit a robbery upon the rights of a woman.

Now the story enters a third scene. This scene too is strange. These angels come to Lut (peace be upon him) in the form of extremely handsome young men. Lut (peace be upon him) also knows that these are dangerous guests: handsome young men, and a people in such a filthy condition. It is inevitable that these people would mistreat these guests. And he is not in a position to defend his guests, so his heart was overcome with this distress, and anxiety and dread took hold of him.

And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account and felt powerless to protect them. The depiction of the punishment of Allah that befell the people of this town is that all of them were destroyed except Lot, his family and the believers. A rain of baked clay stones was rained down upon them. It appears that here the angels of Allah brought about a volcanic action, as a result of which a rain of baked clay stones occurs. And traces of this punishment were preserved so that the people of reason and understanding among later nations might take lesson from it, and even after centuries these traces remain.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 36–37:

وَإِلَىٰ مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْبًا ۔۔۔۔۔۔ دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ (36 – 37)

"And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said: 'O my people, worship Allah and hope for the Last Day, and do not roam the earth committing corruption.' But they denied him, and so a severe earthquake seized them, and they remained lying prostrate in their homes."

This indicates that the call of Islam has been one throughout all eras, and the fundamental creed of the Islamic call has also been one.

﴿اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَارْجُوا الْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ﴾ (29:36) "Worship Allah and hope for the Last Day."

Worshipping the one Allah is the foundation of the Islamic outlook on life, and through hope in the Hereafter it was possible for them to refrain from what they were accumulating in this world, namely unlawful gains, and from cheating in weights and measures. Moreover, they were usurping people's rights and committing highway robbery. Perhaps, out of fear of the Hereafter, they would desist from these crimes. Besides these, they also committed various kinds of oppression against people and used to spread corruption in the land; through fear of the Hereafter their reform could have been achieved.

In short, they eventually denied their Messenger, and God's punishment befell them. In accordance with His established practice regarding those who deny, Allah destroyed them and wiped them off the face of the earth.

﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ﴾ (29:37) "So the severe earthquake seized them, and they remained lying prostrate in their homes." Earlier, the details of this severe earthquake were given, which shook their land to its foundations, and this earthquake came after a fierce shriek that had stunned them, so that people remained lying in the very places where they were. This punishment was inflicted because of their crimes, in which they used to raise cries and clamour, raid people, and plunder them.

Following this, a reference to the destruction of the peoples of 'Ad and Thamud:

﴿And 'Ad and Thamud—We destroyed them, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings. And Satan made their deeds appear pleasing to them and averted them from the way, although they were discerning.﴾ (29:38)

The people of 'Ad lived in the region of al-Ahqaf in the south of the Arabian Peninsula. This region is close to Hadramawt. The Thamud lived in al-Hijr in the north of the Arabian Peninsula, and this area is close to Wadi al-Qura. The people of 'Ad were destroyed by a swift wind storm that could not be controlled, and the people of Thamud by a deadly cry, after which an earthquake came. Their homes were known to the Arabs, and these people passed through these areas during their summer and winter journeys, and they would see their remains, how these nations were reduced to nothing after their honour and power. Here, in this brief allusion, it has been stated what the secret of their misguidance was. This same secret is the reason for the misguidance of all other nations.

﴿And Satan made their deeds appear pleasing to them, and averted them from the way, although they were discerning﴾ (29:37-38). "They were wise." They had the proofs of guidance before them, but Satan, by subjecting them to their carnal desires, made those deeds appear attractive to them. He attacked them through the path that was open: that they were extremely arrogant, took pride in their evil deeds, and because of the strength, wealth and possessions they had gathered through those deeds, those deeds seemed good to them.

﴿And he averted them from the way﴾ (29:38): they had been turned away from the straight path, and this was the only path to faith. Therefore, they lost the opportunities to walk on that path.

﴿And they were discerning﴾ (29:38): they were people of great understanding, possessors of thought and vision, and of the powers of reason and perception.

Now, an allusion to Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman.

Wa Qarun wa Fir'awn... wa ma kanu sabiqin (39)

"And Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman — We destroyed them, and Musa came to them with clear proofs, but they behaved arrogantly in the land, though they were not ones who could escape (Allah's grasp)."

Qarun was a man from the people of Musa, but he rebelled against them because of his wealth. He did not heed the advice of those who counselled him: adopt the path of moderation and humility, do good to people, and do not be insolent or rebellious. Pharaoh was a tyrannical and insolent ruler, and he committed heinous crimes against his people. He had divided them into pieces and held them under complete control. He would kill the men of Bani Israel and let the women live, and this was purely out of oppression. Haman was Pharaoh's minister, and it was he who carried out the implementation of those oppressive and tyrannical state policies. In all of Pharaoh's crimes, he was his helper and supporter. All these people, who possessed power, wealth and the means of life and were fully dominant over the earth, were seized by Allah, because they had put people into trial and used to torment them. And they continued to do this for a long period of time.

"And Allah was not one to wrong them, but they were wronging themselves" (29:41).

After surveying the dreadful and instructive end of the rebels, the arrogant and the oppressors throughout all of human history, and after the mention at the beginning of the surah of the trials and the temptations of misguidance, the discourse now concludes by illustrating, through a parable, the struggle between Islam and disbelief, and between faith and misguidance: that true power is one, and it is the power of Allah. All the powers other than Allah are extremely feeble and fragile. Their example is that of the spider's web. Whoever relies on the spider's web is in fact leaning on something extremely frail. This is the example of all powers besides Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 29, verse 41–43:

Mathal al-ladhina attakhadhu ... wa ma ya'qiluha illa al-'alimun (41–43)

This is a strange and true picture of all the powers that exist in this universe. In it, a reality is highlighted that people generally remain heedless of, and because of this heedlessness their measures and values then change. Then they establish wrong connections. They do not know that they are going in the wrong direction. They cannot make a correct decision about what to take and what to leave.

Because of this wrong thinking, they are then deceived by the power of the state as well. They think that state power is the real power on this earth and that it is everything, and that it is effective everywhere. Therefore they fear this power and remain striving to obtain it. They want to save themselves from the torments of this state power and strive to obtain its support.

Then such people are also deceived by the power of wealth. They think that this is the power through which the values of life are obtained, and that all the values of life are subject to wealth. Thus such people have a desire for acquiring wealth, and they always have fear of the decline of wealth. And they strive at all times for the acquisition of wealth so that through this wealth they may ride upon the necks of people, according to their own conceit.

These people also consider the power of science to be a great power. They regard it too as financial power and the foundation of all powers, through which a person seizes or moves about. Before the power of science too, people bow in the way that science is some deity and people are its servants.

In short, all these apparent powers deceive man. The individuals who possess these powers, the societies that possess these means, or the governments that possess these powers, other people fear them, circle around them, and people sacrifice themselves for them in the way that the moth falls upon the lamp, or the way that it falls into the fire.

Deceived by these apparent powers, man forgets that true power which is the great power that creates these insignificant powers. The One who creates these powers, who is the owner of all these powers, who grants these powers to whomever He wills, who subjugates these powers and turns them in whatever direction He wishes. People forget that taking refuge in these insignificant and apparent powers of the world, whether the powers are in the hands of individuals, or are in some society, or are with some government, is just like someone who relies on a spider's web, or takes refuge in a spider's house. This spider's web is a weak, insignificant and extremely soft cloth; its very structure is weak, and its house too is a weak house. How can it give anyone refuge?

Remember! Support belongs only to the support of Allah, and refuge is only the refuge of Allah, who is a strong Protector. This is a great reality which the Qur'an plants in the hearts of the believing people. And once the Qur'an had planted this reality in the hearts of the people of faith, that group became a powerful group in the world. And it trampled all the apparent powers that stood in its way. It bent the necks of all the tyrants and oppressors of the earth and razed great fortresses to the ground.

How did the Qur'an plant this reality in that group? This reality had settled in every soul. Every heart was filled with it. This reality had mixed into their blood and was running through their veins. This reality was not limited to the utterance of words. Nor was it a topic of discussion over which seminars were held; rather, it was clearly visible in those souls. And in their perception and thought there was nothing else. That God's power is the only power, and God's friendship is the only friendship, and whatever else there is, is weak and feeble. Even though other powers may oppress and tyrannize as much as they can, even though they may have exceeded the limits of oppression and rebellion, even though they may have all the means of seizure and aggression and may be carrying out arrests and crackdowns.

All of this is a spider's house. All these powers and means are a spider's web.

Wa inna awhan ... yaʿlamun (29:41) "And indeed the weakest of houses is the house of the spider, if only they knew."

The callers who are afflicted with trials and tests, who have to face imprisonment and torture and persecution, should reflect on this reality and not let it slip from their sight even for a moment. They have to face various opposing powers in this field. These powers attack them and want to annihilate them. Some powers want to buy them. All these powers are like a spider's web, provided that someone's faith and ideology is firm, and that one knows what the real and true power is.

Inna Allah yaʿlamu ... min shay' (29:42) "Indeed Allah knows whatever they call upon besides Him." These people rely on some other things besides Allah. And Allah knows that these are not things worthy of reliance. Their reality is what was described in the preceding parable, namely the spider's web.

Wa huwa al-ʿAziz al-Hakim (29:42) "And He is the Mighty, the Wise." He is the Dominant, He is the Subduer, He is the Wise, and He is the Manager of this entire universe.

Wa tilka al-amthal ... illa al-ʿalimun (29:43) "And these parables We present to people, but none understand them except those who have knowledge." Some of the polytheists had hearts upon which locks were set and whose intellects were lost; they used to joke with this parable and say that Muhammad's Lord talks about flies and mosquitoes too, and they could not understand the reality described in this parable, nor did it have any effect on them. Therefore Allah said:

Wa ma ya'qiluha illa al-'alimun (29:43) "But only those who have knowledge comprehend them."

"Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. And the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do." (29:45)

Recite the Book before them, for this is the means of Islamic da'wah, a divine miracle, and the truth expounded in this Book is the same truth that is hidden within this universe. And establish prayer: when prayer is established, it restrains from immorality and wrongdoing. It is such a connection with Allah that when someone establishes this connection, he cannot even think of immorality and wrongdoing. It is a means of outward and spiritual purification.
