The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever offers a prayer that does not restrain him from immorality and wrongdoing, his prayer only increases his distance from Allah, and he gains nothing." (Ibn Jarir).

If someone offers such a prayer, we may say that he has performed the prayer, but we cannot say that he has established the prayer. And there is a very great difference between performing prayer and establishing it. When prayer is established, it is the remembrance of Allah, and

"And the remembrance of Allah is greater" (29:45): the remembrance of Allah is great in an absolute sense. It is greater than every thought and every feeling. The remembrance of Allah is greater than every act of worship and every humility.

"And Allah knows what you make" (29:45): nothing is hidden from Him. No matter is confused for Him. In the end you will return to Him, and He will recompense you for all your works.

Lesson No. 182: An Overview

This is the last lesson of Surah al-Ankabut. The first two lessons passed in Juz 20. As we said earlier, the theme of this surah is trial and tribulation. Whoever raises the word of truth faces obstacles. Through the furnace of tribulations and trials, Allah makes the distinction between true and false people clear. Whoever has tasted more of hardship and ease will hold a higher rank. Along with this, it is also impressed upon the mind that the satanic forces on earth, however much they strive to block the path of the believers, have no standing. If the believers are patient and show perseverance, Allah ultimately seizes the wrongdoers in His grip and grants success to the believers. This is the Sunnah of Allah, and the Sunnah of Allah has always been this with Islamic da'wah. From Nuh (peace be upon him) until today, this Sunnah has remained unchanging. It has no alteration or change, and this Sunnah is also linked with the great truth operating in this universe: just as the da'wah of Allah is one and admits no change or alteration, so too the Sunnah of Allah is unchangeable.

The previous lesson ended with the instruction: O Messenger and O believers, recite the revealed verses of Allah that come down to you, study and reflect upon them, and act upon them by establishing prayer, keeping in mind that Allah sees whatever you do.

In this lesson too, the discussion concerns the Book of Allah, and it is explained what relationship exists between this Book and the earlier scriptures. Muslims are advised to deal kindly with the other People of the Book, excluding the wrongdoers, and to converse with them in a good manner. The wrongdoers are those who distorted the Book of Allah, and who replaced the belief in Tawhid with the belief in shirk, and shirk is the greatest wrongdoing. The path and belief of the believers is that Allah is One. All His messengers are one, the books are one, and all books contain the great truth in the sight of Allah, and the believers affirm them.

After this, mention is made of some People of the Book who have come to believe in this last Book, whereas the polytheists of Makkah, from among whom the Final Prophet was chosen, do not believe. They do not value the great honour and great mercy that Allah bestowed upon them. They do not regard as a blessing for themselves the miracle of this Book, its teachings, and the Messenger sent to them, who both speaks to them and recites to them the Word of Allah, whereas before this they had neither read any book nor were they writers. If the Prophet (ﷺ) had been studying books and writing books, there could have been the suspicion that he had composed this Book himself. The polytheists of Makkah, on every occasion, would make the demand: if you are truthful, bring the punishment of Allah with which you threaten us. It is said that this punishment is very near, and that it will encompass you in the form of Hell. It will come on the Day of Resurrection from above and from beneath your feet. It will surround them from every side.

After this, the address turns to the believers who are the target of the persecution of the people of wealth in Makkah. They are advised that if life has been made narrow for them in Makkah, they should migrate so that they may worship the One Lord. This guidance is given in a remarkable manner. The anxieties and apprehensions that arise in their hearts from the thought of migration are removed. All the obstacles that could stand in their path are removed. With a few touches, their inner state is transformed, which shows that the One who revealed this Qur'an is the same Creator who created this universe, because only that Being who created these hearts can produce such an effect in the depths of human hearts and such feelings within them, for He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.

After this, the address turns to the polytheists who are afflicted with ideological confusion. They acknowledge that Allah alone is the Creator of the universe, the Creator of the heavens and earth, the Subjugator of the sun and moon, and that it is He who sends water down from the sky by which this earth is revived after being dead. When they are on a sea voyage, they call upon Allah alone. But after that, they again begin to commit shirk. They deny the truth of the Book of Allah, inflict unjust torments on the Messenger of Allah, and throw the believers into trials and calamities. The polytheists are also reminded: see, for you this sanctuary has been made a place of security in which you live in peace, while all the tribes around you live in constant fear and dread. Yet despite this, these polytheists fabricate lies against Allah and associate with Allah self-invented deities. Therefore they are threatened that you will be cast into Hell and will remain there forever.

The surah concludes with the promise that Allah will show the believers the paths to success, but only to those believers who are sincere, who have crossed the obstacles, who have passed through trials, and who have mastered the difficulties of the path, even though the obstacles on this path are many, and they have accomplished this difficult task.

Lesson No. 182: Explanation of the Verses

45 to 69

"Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do. And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except for those of them who commit wrongdoing, and say: 'We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you. Our God and your God is one, and to Him we are Muslims [submitting]'" (29:46)

The da'wah that began with Nuh (peace be upon him) and concluded with the Prophet (ﷺ) is one single da'wah, from one single Lord, and its purpose and objective are also one: to bring back misguided humanity and place it upon the path of the Lord of the worlds, so that it may live in accordance with the guidance and methodology of Allah. Those who have believed in the da'wah of the earlier messengers are brothers of the believers. All are one nation, worshipping one God. Humanity, in every age and every time and place, has been divided into two groups. One group is of the believers, called Hizb Allah, and the other group is of the enemies of Allah, called Hizb al-Shayatin. In this arrangement, no difference has ever arisen across any time or place. Therefore, from ancient times until today, the believers are one party and the disbelievers are one party.

This is a great and lofty truth upon which Islam stands, and which is defined in this verse. This truth elevates the relationships between one human being and another above mere blood, lineage, nationality, homeland, trade and interests, and establishes them on the foundation of the One God. The faith of all humanity should be based on a way of life in which people of all colours and all races melt together. All nationalities, whether racial or territorial, should come to an end, and in which the distances of time and place disappear, and all humanity holds fast to one strong rope: the rope of the Creator and Lawgiver of the universe.

This is why here the Muslims are forbidden from debate and dispute with the People of the Book, except that the debate be conducted in the most excellent manner. The Muslims are told what the nature of the relationship is between their religion and the teachings and messengerships of the earlier messengers, and that the Muslims should be content with the final form of this historical Islamic da'wah, namely the religion of Islam, which is in agreement with all earlier da'wahs, and which is the completion of all earlier da'wahs and messengerships. This final form has been given to it by the knowledge and wisdom of Allah, who knows the interests of human beings better than human beings themselves.

"Except those of them who commit wrongdoing" (29:46): those who deviated from Tawhid, which is the cornerstone of the Islamic way of life, who associated partners with Allah, and who abandoned Islam as a way of life. For there is neither leniency for such people nor any need for dialogue with them. It was against such wrongdoers that Islam waged war when the Islamic state was established in Madinah. Some people have accused the Prophet (ﷺ) of this: that when the polytheists in Makkah were treating him harshly, he said these things, that kindness and goodness should be adopted towards the People of the Book, but when his government was established in Madinah, he began disputing with the People of the Book, fought wars, and adopted conduct contrary to the Makkan sayings. This is a great slander, and this very Makkan verse refutes it. Islam permits gentle treatment only towards those People of the Book who are not wrongdoers and not polytheists, who remain upon their original religion, and who are upon correct Tawhid in accordance with the guidance of the earlier messengers.

"And say: We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you, and our God and your God is one, and to Him we are Muslims" (29:46). Therefore there is no need for argument and disagreement, and wrangling is out of place. We all acknowledge the One Allah as God. The believers believe in the Qur'an and also believe in the Book of the earlier prophets, because Islam is one chain, and all the prophethoods are its links.

"Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. And the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do." (29:45)

Recite the Book before them, for this is the means of Islamic da'wah, a divine miracle, and the truth expounded in this Book is the same truth that is hidden within this universe. And establish prayer: when prayer is established, it restrains from immorality and wrongdoing. It is such a connection with Allah that when someone establishes this connection, he cannot even think of immorality and wrongdoing. It is a means of outward and spiritual purification. Therefore no filth, impurity or dirt can cling to it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever offers a prayer that does not restrain him from immorality and wrongdoing, his prayer only increases his distance from Allah, and he gains nothing." (Ibn Jarir).

If someone offers such a prayer, we may say that he has performed the prayer, but we cannot say that he has established the prayer. And there is a very great difference between performing prayer and establishing it. When prayer is established, it is the remembrance of Allah, and

"And the remembrance of Allah is greater" (29:45): the remembrance of Allah is great in an absolute sense. It is greater than every thought and every feeling. The remembrance of Allah is greater than every act of worship and every humility.

"And Allah knows what you make" (29:45): nothing is hidden from Him. No matter is confused for Him. In the end you will return to Him, and He will recompense you for all your works.

Lesson No. 182: An Overview

This is the last lesson of Surah al-Ankabut. The first two lessons passed in Juz 20. As we said earlier, the theme of this surah is trial and tribulation. Whoever raises the word of truth faces obstacles. Through the furnace of tribulations and trials, Allah makes the distinction between true and false people clear. Whoever has tasted more of hardship and ease will hold a higher rank. Along with this, it is also impressed upon the mind that the satanic forces on earth, however much they strive to block the path of the believers, have no standing. If the believers are patient and show perseverance, Allah ultimately seizes the wrongdoers in His grip and grants success to the believers. This is the Sunnah of Allah, and the Sunnah of Allah has always been this with Islamic da'wah. From Nuh (peace be upon him) until today, this Sunnah has remained unchanging. It has no alteration or change, and this Sunnah is also linked with the great truth operating in this universe: just as the da'wah of Allah is one and admits no change or alteration, so too the Sunnah of Allah is unchangeable.

The previous lesson ended with the instruction: O Messenger and O believers, recite the revealed verses of Allah that come down to you, study and reflect upon them, and act upon them by establishing prayer, keeping in mind that Allah sees whatever you do.

In this lesson too, the discussion concerns the Book of Allah, and it is explained what relationship exists between this Book and the earlier scriptures. Muslims are advised to deal kindly with the other People of the Book, excluding the wrongdoers, and to converse with them in a good manner. The wrongdoers are those who distorted the Book of Allah, and who replaced the belief in Tawhid with the belief in shirk, and shirk is the greatest wrongdoing. The path and belief of the believers is that Allah is One. All His messengers are one, the books are one, and all books contain the great truth in the sight of Allah, and the believers affirm them.

After this, mention is made of some People of the Book who have come to believe in this last Book, whereas the polytheists of Makkah, from among whom the Final Prophet was chosen, do not believe. They do not value the great honour and great mercy that Allah bestowed upon them. They do not regard as a blessing for themselves the miracle of this Book, its teachings, and the Messenger sent to them, who both speaks to them and recites to them the Word of Allah, whereas before this they had neither read any book nor were they writers. If the Prophet (ﷺ) had been studying books and writing books, there could have been the suspicion that he had composed this Book himself. The polytheists of Makkah, on every occasion, would make the demand: if you are truthful, bring the punishment of Allah with which you threaten us. It is said that this punishment is very near, and that it will encompass you in the form of Hell. It will come on the Day of Resurrection from above and from beneath your feet. It will surround them from every side.

After this, the address turns to the believers who are the target of the persecution of the people of wealth in Makkah. They are advised that if life has been made narrow for them in Makkah, they should migrate so that they may worship the One Lord. This guidance is given in a remarkable manner. The anxieties and apprehensions that arise in their hearts from the thought of migration are removed. All the obstacles that could stand in their path are removed. With a few touches, their inner state is transformed, which shows that the One who revealed this Qur'an is the same Creator who created this universe, because only that Being who created these hearts can produce such an effect in the depths of human hearts and such feelings within them, for He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.

After this, the address turns to the polytheists who are afflicted with ideological confusion. They acknowledge that Allah alone is the Creator of the universe, the Creator of the heavens and earth, the Subjugator of the sun and moon, and that it is He who sends water down from the sky by which this earth is revived after being dead. When they are on a sea voyage, they call upon Allah alone. But after that, they again begin to commit shirk. They deny the truth of the Book of Allah, inflict unjust torments on the Messenger of Allah, and throw the believers into trials and calamities. The polytheists are also reminded: see, for you this sanctuary has been made a place of security in which you live in peace, while all the tribes around you live in constant fear and dread. Yet despite this, these polytheists fabricate lies against Allah and associate with Allah self-invented deities. Therefore they are threatened that you will be cast into Hell and will remain there forever.

The surah concludes with the promise that Allah will show the believers the paths to success, but only to those believers who are sincere, who have crossed the obstacles, who have passed through trials, and who have mastered the difficulties of the path, even though the obstacles on this path are many, and they have accomplished this difficult task.

Lesson No. 182: Explanation of the Verses

45 to 69

"Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do. And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except for those of them who commit wrongdoing, and say: 'We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you. Our God and your God is one, and to Him we are Muslims [submitting]'" (29:46)

The da'wah that began with Nuh (peace be upon him) and concluded with the Prophet (ﷺ) is one single da'wah, from one single Lord, and its purpose and objective are also one: to bring back misguided humanity and place it upon the path of the Lord of the worlds, so that it may live in accordance with the guidance and methodology of Allah. Those who have believed in the da'wah of the earlier messengers are brothers of the believers. All are one nation, worshipping one God. Humanity, in every age and every time and place, has been divided into two groups. One group is of the believers, called Hizb Allah, and the other group is of the enemies of Allah, called Hizb al-Shayatin. In this arrangement, no difference has ever arisen across any time or place. Therefore, from ancient times until today, the believers are one party and the disbelievers are one party.

This is a great and lofty truth upon which Islam stands, and which is defined in this verse. This truth elevates the relationships between one human being and another above mere blood, lineage, nationality, homeland, trade and interests, and establishes them on the foundation of the One God. The faith of all humanity should be based on a way of life in which people of all colours and all races melt together. All nationalities, whether racial or territorial, should come to an end, and in which the distances of time and place disappear, and all humanity holds fast to one strong rope: the rope of the Creator and Lawgiver of the universe.

This is why here the Muslims are forbidden from debate and dispute with the People of the Book, except that the debate be conducted in the most excellent manner. The Muslims are told what the nature of the relationship is between their religion and the teachings and messengerships of the earlier messengers, and that the Muslims should be content with the final form of this historical Islamic da'wah, namely the religion of Islam, which is in agreement with all earlier da'wahs, and which is the completion of all earlier da'wahs and messengerships. This final form has been given to it by the knowledge and wisdom of Allah, who knows the interests of human beings better than human beings themselves.

"Except those of them who commit wrongdoing" (29:46): those who deviated from Tawhid, which is the cornerstone of the Islamic way of life, who associated partners with Allah, and who abandoned Islam as a way of life. For there is neither leniency for such people nor any need for dialogue with them. It was against such wrongdoers that Islam waged war when the Islamic state was established in Madinah. Some people have accused the Prophet (ﷺ) of this: that when the polytheists in Makkah were treating him harshly, he said these things, that kindness and goodness should be adopted towards the People of the Book, but when his government was established in Madinah, he began disputing with the People of the Book, fought wars, and adopted conduct contrary to the Makkan sayings. This is a great slander, and this very Makkan verse refutes it. Islam permits gentle treatment only towards those People of the Book who are not wrongdoers and not polytheists, who remain upon their original religion, and who are upon correct Tawhid in accordance with the guidance of the earlier messengers.

"And say: We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you, and our God and your God is one, and to Him we are Muslims" (29:46). Therefore there is no need for argument and disagreement, and wrangling is out of place. We all acknowledge the One Allah as God. The believers believe in the Qur'an and also believe in the Book of the earlier prophets, because Islam is one chain, and all the prophethoods are its links.

"Thus" — that is, in accordance with one continuous and historically consistent method, in accordance with one divine law (sunnah ilahiyyah) which is unchangeable, and in the same manner through which Allah has always guided the messengers.

﴿Thus We have sent down to you the Book﴾ (29:47). O Prophet (ﷺ), We have sent down the Book to you in this same way. And when the Book was sent down, people were divided into two groups in response to it. One group were those who were from among the People of the Book and also from among the Quraysh; they believed. The second group are those who, even after the People of the Book had believed and borne witness to it, still do not accept it, although they have already confirmed its truth.

﴿And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers﴾ (29:47). That is, these verses are so clear and so straightforward that only one whose intellect has been veiled, whose soul has been covered, and who has become incapable of seeing the truth, can deny them. The true meaning of kufr (disbelief) is indeed concealing and placing under veils. Here, in the manner of expression that the Qur'an has adopted, both the technical meaning of kufr and its lexical meaning have been kept in view.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 48:

﴿And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you write it with your right hand, for then would have doubted the falsifiers.﴾ (Qur'an 29:48)

The Qur'an pursues the doubts of the disbelievers to the point that even their childish objections and suspicions are answered. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spent the longest part of his life among the disbelievers of Makkah. He could neither read nor write. Suddenly they were presented with such a strange book that it left all the learned people and writers powerless. Had the Prophet (ﷺ) been literate before the revelation of the Qur'an, the disbelievers of Makkah would have had a justified basis for objecting that the Prophet (ﷺ) was himself composing it, and therefore their present objections would be baseless. I say that the Qur'an also answers their frivolous and childish questions. Otherwise, even if it were assumed that the Prophet (ﷺ) was literate, there would still have been no justification for them to doubt the Qur'an. This is because, if the Qur'an is considered on its own, it is a miraculous book and not a book composed by human beings. It is beyond the bounds of human power and understanding. Its subjects lie beyond the limits of human knowledge and perception. The truth recorded in the Qur'an is an unconditioned truth, just as the truth existing within this universe is unconditioned. Whenever a person reflects upon the texts of the Qur'an, he comes to know that behind the Qur'an there is immense power. There is also a great majesty in the worship of the Qur'an, and this power and this majesty are beyond the capacity of human speech.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 49:

"Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge, and none denies Our signs except the wrongdoers." This Qur'an consists of clear proofs for people of knowledge, in which there is no confusion or complexity, nor any doubt or uncertainty. These are proofs that exist in people's breasts; people's hearts are content with these proofs, so people of knowledge do not seek any further proof for the verses of the Qur'an. That knowledge to which the word "knowledge" can be applied exists in the hearts of these people. It sits there in the form of a established disposition (malakah). It gushes forth from hearts, it guides hearts, and takes them straight to the destination.

"And none denies Our signs except the wrongdoers" (29:49). Those who do not assess reality and matters correctly, and who, leaving the straight path, walk on crooked roads.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 50:

They say, "Why are no signs sent down upon him from his Lord?" Say, "Signs are only with Allah, and I am only a plain warner."

By these miracles and signs are meant the miracles and signs which the prophets presented before people at the dawn of humanity, in the childhood era of mankind, namely material miracles. These miracles were a proof only for those who witnessed them. The prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, however, is the final and everlasting prophethood, which is a proof for all those people to whom its call reaches, and this prophethood will continue for as long as humanity exists and this world stands. For this reason, Allah has given this prophethood a miraculous Book which is recited forever, and whose miraculous nature never ends, and whose excellences and wonders never come to an end. For Allah, a separate treasury of the treasures of the Qur'an continuously becomes manifest, and its miracles and proofs remain present in the hearts of the people of knowledge of every age. Whenever the people of knowledge reflect upon it, they find the miraculous nature and wonders of this Book, and they clearly perceive from what source the Holy Qur'an has received this greatness and majesty.

"Say, signs are only with Allah" (29:50). Allah manifests His signs at the time when there is need and necessity for them. All these matters proceed according to Allah's system of planning and decree, therefore I can neither make any proposal in this regard nor make any demand. This is neither befitting for me nor is it my habit.

"And I am only a plain warner" (29:50). I warn and caution, and I clearly explain the realities to people, and this is my duty, which I fulfil. Whatever happens after this will be according to Allah's decree and planning.

In this way, Allah purifies the Islamic worldview from every doubt and suspicion. The limits of the station and rank of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are defined. A distinction is made between the attributes of the Messenger ﷺ and the attributes of the One, Irresistible God. In this way, the clouds of doubt that had gathered around the personalities of those messengers who were given material miracles are dispelled from around the personality of the Messenger ﷺ, because the attributes of earlier messengers had been mixed with divine attributes, and people had surrounded the personalities of those messengers with illusions and superstitions, as a result of which a great deviation occurred in their beliefs.

Those who are demanding material miracles have not understood this matter well, nor have they been able to grasp its importance, that Allah has done them a great favour by sending down the Qur'an.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 51:

﴿و لم يكفهم ... لقوم يؤمنون﴾ (29:51)

This is their ingratitude for the blessings and mercies of Allah, although Allah's favours become manifest through gratitude and appreciation. Is it not sufficient for them that they should ascend to the heavens with this Qur'an and see that it is being sent down from the heavens, and that, coming from the heavens, it is touching the strings of their hearts? It speaks of their hearts. It speaks of their surroundings. It makes them aware that Allah's gaze is upon them at all times. Your affairs are of such importance with Allah that He discusses them with you; He relates stories to you. Yet, O human being, you are weaker and smaller than a mosquito in this vast universe of Allah. Indeed, O human being, your earth, your sun and your moon are in Allah's universe as a mere straw is in comparison to this earth, and even this straw is within Allah's power. Nevertheless, Allah has honoured you, and He sends down this Qur'an from the heights of the heavens, yet you still do not value it?

﴿Inna fi dhalika ... yu'minun﴾ (29:51) "Indeed in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe." This is because only those who believe can feel that mercy and compassion, and only they can become aware of how much mercy and compassion Allah showed His servants by sending down the Qur'an. Only such people can understand that Allah, who is exalted in rank and full of greatness, invites this insignificant human being to His own table. Only such people can benefit from this Qur'an, for it is the water of life for the one who studies it, and through it the doors of boundless treasures open for the believer and the one who reflects, and this Qur'an creates light and radiance within their souls.

Those who have not been given awareness of these matters seek crude material miracles, and they wish to prove this great and eternal miracle through trivial miracles. Their personalities have been distorted, so their hearts do not open to this light. Therefore, do not waste your time on such people. Leave their matter to Allah; He alone will decide their case.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 52–55:

Say: "Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you." ... "Those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah, it is they who are the losers" (29:52).

Who could be a greater witness than the One who knows everything about the worlds? Allah bears witness by His knowledge that these people are upon falsehood. As for "those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah, they are the losers" (29:52): they are losers absolutely. They have been deprived of everything. They have lost both this world and the Hereafter. They have been deprived of their dignity, their personality, guidance, steadfastness, tranquility, truthfulness and light.

Belief in the Being of Allah is also an action and an earning. It is in itself a good earning, and Allah rewards it out of His grace and bounty. The reward is this: through faith, the heart attains tranquility and the paths of life become defined. Whatever events occur in this life, the believing servant accepts them with a cheerful countenance; he relies upon Allah, seeks and hopes for the support of Allah, and has certainty of a good end. This itself is an acquisition, an earning, of which the disbelievers are deprived.

"It is they who are the losers" (29:52).

Now the discussion of the polytheists moves forward: they hasten the coming of the punishment, although Hell is very close to them.

"They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers. On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, He will say, 'Taste what you used to do'" (29:53–55).

The polytheists heard from the Prophet ﷺ verses of warning and intimidation, but they could not grasp the wisdom of why, despite their disbelief, this punishment was not being sent down upon them. Therefore, being bold because of this respite, they would demand the punishment from the Prophet ﷺ as a challenge. Yet it often happens that Allah grants criminals respite to go beyond bounds, so that they reach the final limits of rebellion and corruption. Then the punishment comes. Or this respite is prolonged so that Allah may test the believers, so that they become exceedingly steadfast and firm in faith, and so that the one who lacks patience and perseverance may be removed from their ranks. Or this respite is given because Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware, and He knows that among the ranks of the disbelievers there are still people who will seek the paths of truth and come to guidance, or that from the progeny of these people there are going to be born those who will attain the path of guidance. They will join the party of Allah, even if their parents are polytheists. Beyond these, there may be other wisdoms of Allah which He alone knows and which are hidden from us.

These polytheists did not possess the understanding and perception to grasp these wisdoms and plans of Allah. Therefore, in a spirit of defiance and as a challenge, they demanded the punishment. But:

"And had there not been a appointed term, the punishment would have come upon them" (29:53). Thus, in the midst of explaining this wisdom, Allah warns them that the punishment for which they are impatient will come upon them suddenly, at a time when you will not expect it, and when it comes suddenly they will be stunned and bewildered.

"And it will surely come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive it" (29:53).

Later, on the battlefield of Badr, this punishment came upon them. The word of Allah proved true. They saw with their own eyes how true Allah's promise is. Allah did not send down upon them a comprehensive and all-encompassing punishment like that which came upon the earlier nations, nor did He accept their demand for the manifestation of material miracles as He had accepted the demand of earlier nations to be shown miracles. They denied, and a comprehensive punishment came upon them. They were annihilated, because among them were people who, according to the knowledge of Allah, were going to believe in a later time, who were going to become the finest members of the Islamic army, and from whose descendants were going to be born people who would hold aloft the banner of Islam for a long period in later ages. All this was to happen according to the plan and decree of Allah, and it did happen.

"They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers" (29:54). This is the Qur'an's distinctive and remarkably forceful mode of expression, in which it gives the future promised event the form of a present reality. Such a vivid depiction is made here, as though Hell has already encompassed the disbelievers, although it is still hidden behind the veils of the future. Yet in terms of their deeds, it is an actuality which has already been witnessed and which appears on the screens of human perception. These people should refrain from issuing such a dangerous challenge. Do those hasten who are already encompassed by Hell, which can at any moment tighten its grip and seize them? Now, what will their condition be there, for which they are hastening so eagerly?

"On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He will say, 'Taste what you used to do'" (29:55). This will be a most terrifying scene. In a most dreadful state, they will be rebuked with this sarcastic reproach.

"Taste what you used to do" (29:55). This is the outcome of that haste and impatience which you used to show, and of your giving no weight to those who warned you.

Here the discourse leaves the deniers, the rejecters and those who transgress limits in a painful scene of punishment that encircles them from above and below. Now the address turns toward the believers, upon whom these deniers inflict persecution merely because of beliefs and ideas, and whom they prevent from worshipping their Lord. They are told that the earth of Allah is vast; take your religion and your beliefs and settle elsewhere. This counsel is given in a most affectionate, fresh and deeply effective manner. Such a melody strikes all the strings of the heart and sets them vibrating.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 56–60:

O My servants who believe... and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (56–60)

The Creator of hearts, the One who knows the secret thoughts of hearts, the ideas that come into hearts, the whisperings that arise in hearts and the apprehensions hidden within hearts, and the Creator of the universe who created those hearts, calls out: "O My servants who believe." With these words the believers are invited to migrate in the way of Allah. Through this address, at the very first stage, it is made clear what the reality of this migration is: that it is the relocation of His servants for the sake of Allah, their Lord, and in the way of their Gracious Master. This was the first point; the second feeling that is instilled in them is the following.

"Indeed, My earth is spacious" (29:56). "You are My servants and this is My earth, and it is very spacious, so spacious that it can give you a place. Why, then, do you remain stuck in the narrow confines of Makkah, where you are persecuted merely because of your religion, your beliefs and your ideology? Here you are not even permitted to worship your Lord and Gracious Master. Bid farewell to these constraints and go out into Allah's wide world. Take your religion with you, escape this oppression, so that you may freely worship your Lord." "So worship Me alone" (29:56).

When a person is persuaded to leave his homeland, the first pain that stirs in his heart is the pain of leaving his country. For this reason Allah adopts such a gentle manner here: "O My servants who believe, indeed My earth is spacious. Makkah is Mine and Madinah is Mine. The entire earth is Mine. Therefore, love only that land in which you can worship Me and in which there is room for you." The second thought that arises on such occasions is the fear and apprehension of the dangers of migration, namely that if they leave their homes, death may overtake them on the road. Especially in such circumstances, when the disbelievers had confined the Muslims in Makkah and would not even permit them to leave there, setting out on the path of migration was also perilous. Therefore Allah removes this apprehension as well:

"Every soul shall taste death. Then to Us you will be returned" (29:57). As for death, it comes to every place, so do not be concerned about it, especially since the time and cause of death are known to no one. All must return to Allah. These people are migrants, and even if they did not migrate, they would still be returned to Allah, and you are the servants of Allah; in both this world and the Hereafter you are to turn to Allah alone. So what is there to fear in this matter, or what place is there for fear and dread in the heart? Moreover, Allah's concern is not merely that He will give you the expanses of the earth in this world and you will be safe; rather, the resting place prepared for you in the Hereafter is far greater. Now you are leaving your homeland, so you will receive vastness in this world too; and you are leaving your house, so in Paradise mansions are prepared for you, far greater and more magnificent than those little dwellings of yours.

"As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, We shall certainly settle them in lofty mansions of Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever" (29:58). They will be welcomed there with these words, and their struggle will be mentioned.

"How excellent is the reward of those who work, those who have been patient and who put their trust in their Lord" (29:59). Thus the believers are being urged to migrate, promises are being made to them, and from the atmosphere of anxiety, apprehension and fear they are being taught steadfastness, courage and resolve.

Naturally, at the time of migration the concern also arises that a person has a stomach to fill. How will the needs of morning and evening be met? One leaves one's homeland, one leaves one's wealth, one abandons one's livelihood and departs. Here in Makkah, at least, the provision of life's necessities is assured; every person is engaged in some livelihood. Thus an answer is given to these apprehensions as well.

"And how many a creature there is that does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" (29:60). This is an occurrence that opens a person's eyes, and we see this reality with our own eyes day and night. There are creatures that do not carry their provision around, do not gather it, and make no arrangements for it. They do not even know what plan they should make to produce that provision, nor do they know how to store it. Yet Allah provides for all of them; no creature has ever died of hunger. Likewise Allah provides for people too. Although some people fall into the illusion that they produce their own sustenance, the reality is that Allah alone supplies these means of sustenance, and these means are in fact the provision itself. If these means created by Allah did not exist, a human being could do nothing at all. Therefore, by migrating you will not die of hunger. Do not worry about it; you are the servants of Allah, and Allah makes arrangements for His servants wherever they may be, just as He makes arrangements for His other creation and never lets anyone die of hunger.

These songs of loving affection conclude with the awareness that Allah is with the believers. He always keeps His gracious regard upon them; He hears all their words, knows their circumstances, and never leaves them alone.

"And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" (29:60). If this passage ends here, in this state Allah has removed all the apprehensions present in the hearts of the migrants, and all the misgivings that stir in the heart when setting out in the way of Allah have been dispelled; the anxieties and fears that were in the hearts of the believers have now been replaced by tranquility. Instead of distress and worries, they are now content, and the hearts of the believers have attained such peace, steadiness and firmness that they consider themselves secure in nearness to Allah, under His watch and in His protection. Who is there that can perceive a human being's apprehensions in this manner and remove them in this way, other than the Creator of the universe, who knows all those things that pass through hearts?

After this brief dialogue with the believers, the address turns back to the contradictory thoughts of the polytheists. Their notions are so unreasonable that on the one hand they acknowledge that it is Allah alone who created the heavens and the earth, who has subjected the sun and the moon, who sends down rain from the sky and revives the earth after it has died, and that it is He who expands and restricts provision. When they are in extreme fear, they call upon Allah alone. Yet after accepting these things, they associate others with Allah in worship. Those who call upon Allah alone and worship Him, these people persecute them. Although they acknowledge Allah, they unjustly inflict oppression upon such people. They forget the favours Allah bestowed upon them, and they terrify the servants of Allah within the Sacred House.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 61–63:

ولئن سالتھم من خلق السموت والارض ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ جھنم مثوی للکفرین (61 – 67)

"And this worldly life is nothing but a game and a diversion of the heart. Indeed, the real life is the abode of the Hereafter; if only they knew. When they board a ship, they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting their religion to Him; but when He brings them safely to land, behold, they associate partners with Him, so as to be ungrateful for what We have given them, and so that they may enjoy themselves. But they will soon come to know. Do they not see that We made a secure sanctuary, while people are snatched away from around them? Do they then believe in falsehood and deny the blessing of Allah? Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?"

These verses depict the beliefs of the Arabs before the advent of Islam. From this it becomes clear that the original beliefs of the Arabs were based on Tawhid. In later periods, deviation entered their beliefs and ideas. This is not surprising, since they were the descendants of Isma'il. They claimed that they were upon the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham), and therefore they attributed their beliefs to Isma'il and Ibrahim (peace be upon them). These people gave no importance to the religion of Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus) (peace be upon them). These religions existed around the Arabian Peninsula, because these people, considering the religion of Ibrahim superior, took pride in it. But they could not understand how far their beliefs had deviated from the original religion, and in practice they had become polytheists.

When they are asked who created the heavens and the earth, who subjected the sun and the moon, who sends down water from the sky, and who brings forth vegetation from the earth after it is dead, they plainly acknowledge that Allah is the one who does all this. Yet despite this, they worship their idols, they worship the jinn, they worship the angels, and they associate all of them with Allah in worship, while they do not associate them with Him in creation. This was a strange contradiction. Because of this contradiction, in these verses Allah expresses His astonishment at their way of thinking:

﴿Fa-anna yu'fakun﴾ (29:61): "Then how are you being deluded?" That is, how have you turned away from the truth and become caught up in these confused beliefs.

﴿Bal aktharuhum la ya'qilun﴾ (29:63): "But most of them do not understand," because one whose sound intellect is intact does not adopt such beliefs.

Between the question about the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the question about the One who subjected the sun and the moon, the question about the One who sends down water from the sky, and the question about the One who makes the dead earth green, it is also established that it is Allah who constricts the provision of one and expands it for another. Thus, alongside all the signs of His power, it was also made clear that He is the Provider, and that Allah knows all creatures and provides sustenance to all.

﴿Inna Allaha bikulli shay'in 'alim﴾ (29:62): "Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things."

Provision is clearly linked with the movement of the heavens. Water, life, and vegetation are also linked with the motion of the celestial spheres. Likewise, the expansion and constriction of provision are in Allah's hand. All these phenomena are clearly displayed in these verses. Provision comes into being through water. Rivers and streams flow from rain, and through them life and vegetation are sustained. This water is stored within the earth and also flows upon it, and through it the game of land and sea comes into being. In short, all provisions are connected with waters. Waters come into existence according to the laws of nature of this universe, and all phenomena of the sun and moon occur as a result of the subjugation of the sun and moon. Moreover, if these laws of nature changed even slightly, this very face of the earth's surface would change at once. Then, all the reserves and natural resources within the earth also conform to the laws of time and space established by Allah. All these varieties of the earth are the result of the movement of the sun and moon (we have given details in Part 19 of Fi Zilal).

The Qur'an presents this great universe and its observable scenes as proof and evidence. The point of reflection in the truth that the Qur'an brings is this great universe. A thoughtful and reflective heart certainly contemplates this great universe. Seeing the wonders of this universe, it remains alive and awake, and understands the craftsmanship of the Hand of Power. It is aware of the unshakeable law of nature that has been established for this vast universe. With a very calm heart, with great seriousness, and with great ease, it attains this awareness. It does not even need very deep contemplation; and whenever this living and awakened heart finds some sign among the great signs of this universe, it becomes full of praise of Allah.

﴿Qul al-hamdu lillah, bal aktharuhum la ya'lamun﴾ (29:63): "Say: All praise is for Allah; but most of them do not know." On the basis of the signs of life upon the earth and the constriction and expansion of provision, a sensitive scale of the values of life is placed before human beings, so that they may see that this worldly life, with all its varieties and its play and amusement, is a fleeting spectacle. The real life is the life of the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 65:

﴿Then, when they board a ship...﴾ to ﴿...behold, they associate partners with Him﴾ (29:65–66). This too is a very great contradiction in their beliefs. Their beliefs are so unsteady that when they are on the deep sea in a ship, and the vessel becomes a plaything amid the surging of the ocean waves, and fear overcomes them, they call upon none but Allah. At that moment they come to realize that true power belongs to Allah alone. Then in their thinking too Allah is alone, and on their tongues too the name of Allah alone is found. Now they follow that nature of theirs which is aware of the Oneness of God. But when Allah brings them safely to dry land, these people suddenly return to associating partners with Him, and that natural awareness is again suppressed. Suddenly they forget the state in which they called upon Allah alone, and after acknowledgment and submission they once again fall into the path of shirk.

What is the outcome of this straying and misguidance? It is that these people become ungrateful and disbelieving of the blessings that Allah has bestowed upon them. These people deviate from the natural path that Allah has placed within their very being. They disregard the natural proofs which they perceive, and they forget that the life of this world is merely a provision for a limited time, but they will very soon learn their true end. That will be a very evil end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 66:

لیکفروا بما ۔۔۔۔۔ یعلمون (29:66) — "So that they may deny what We have given them, and that they may enjoy themselves; but they will come to know." This is an extremely severe warning, that of an unknown calamity. "They will soon come to know." After this, Allah reminds them: behold, Allah has given you this "Sanctuary of Security" (ḥaram āmin), within which you live in utmost peace and tranquility. Will you not then give thanks for this great blessing of Allah, by worshipping Allah alone and calling upon Him alone? Rather, on the contrary, within this Sanctuary of Security you frighten and distress the believers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verse 67:

اولم یروا انا جعلنا ۔۔۔۔۔۔ یکفرون (29: 67)

The condition of the people of Makkah was that they lived in extreme peace and security because of the sacred Haram of Makkah. People honored them because of the House of Allah (Bayt Allah). The Arab tribes around them would kill one another, and in each of them there was fear of the others. If they found security, it was under the shade of the House of Allah. And this security was given by Allah, but it was a very great ingratitude that these people turned the House of Allah into a den of idols, and that the worship of other than Allah continued within the House of Allah.

﴿Have they not seen that We made a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched away all around them? Will they then believe in falsehood and deny the blessings of Allah?﴾

افبالباطل ۔۔۔۔۔۔ یکفرون (29: 67) "Do they then believe in falsehood and deny the favours of Allah?"

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 29, verses 68–69:

{ Wa man azlamu … mathwan lil-kafirin } (29:68) The people of Makkah have already committed this crime. They have fabricated a lie against Allah by claiming that Allah has Himself appointed partners with Him. The truth came to them, and they denied it. Apart from the abode of Hell, what place do such people deserve? And the truth came to them, and they denied it. Apart from the abode of Hell, what other place do such people deserve? Certainly such people deserve Hell.

The conclusion of the Surah is a portrayal of the opposing party to the disbelievers. These are the people who strove in the paths of Allah so that they might reach Allah and their connection with Allah might be established. Despite enduring unbearable hardships in the way of Allah, they neither broke their covenant nor lost hope. They overcame the desires of the self and also bore the oppression of people. They took up their burdens and set out upon that long journey with those burdens, which was both lengthy and laborious. Allah does not leave such people alone in this journey, nor does He waste their faith, nor does He forget their struggle. Allah is watching them from His exalted Throne, and He is greatly pleased with them. He sees them and guides them at every step. He will observe their efforts and take their hands, setting them upon the right path. Their patience and their purity are being observed, and He is the Giver of the very best reward.
